LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of writing, part of Strand 9 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to punctuate texts appropriately?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search for and share with peers hyphenated and unhyphenated words such as dark-blue shirt, good- looking, goodhearted, fast-moving, anticlockwise from the internet, magazines, newspapers, textbooks or brochures,

2. listen to a dictation of the following words: mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in law and write them down,

3. listen to an audio recording of the words mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in-law and anti- clockwise and create a list,

4. use words such as fast-flowing, slow- moving, open-mouthed, big-eyed, sugar-free among others in sentences,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search for and share with peers hyphenated and unhyphenated words such as dark-blue shirt, good- looking, goodhearted, fast-moving, anticlockwise from the internet, magazines, newspapers, textbooks or brochures,
2. listen to a dictation of the following words: mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in law and write them down,
3. listen to an audio recording of the words mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in-law and anti- clockwise and create a list,
4. use words such as fast-flowing, slow- moving, open-mouthed, big-eyed, sugar-free among others in sentences,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and efficiently is promoted as the learner punctuates and

hyphenates words correctly.

• Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to interact with technological devices is enhanced as they view videos on

the internet and explain how the hyphen is used.

83

Values:
• Social Justice: This is fostered in the learner as non-discrimination is encouraged while searching for, and sharing

with peers on hyphenated words.

• Unity: This is displayed in the team spirit that is inculcated in the learner as they work with peers to create a

poster on lifestyle diseases.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle Diseases: The learner’s general health and wellbeing is improved as they interact with, and gain knowledge

on lifestyle diseases while creating posters featuring the target words.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the learning of punctuation marks (the hyphen) to correct punctuation of texts in

Agriculture.
